name: PA-05
label: Safe D

key_factors: Strong Democratic district with +15 partisan lean
Scanlon's large fundraising edge over near-zero-spending challenger
Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~98%
No polls or expert ratings, so uncertainty stays elevated
model.rationale: The fundamentals point firmly to Scanlon: a +15 Democratic lean, incumbency, and a roughly 100-to-1 fundraising advantage over Nicholas Manganaro, with markets pricing a Democratic win near certain. With no polls or expert ratings available, the forecast stays close to the fundamentals-based margin of about 23 points.
model.watch: Any late polling showing a much tighter race, or a major national shift toward Republicans, would be the main reason to revisit this rating.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Incumbent Mary Gay Scanlon (D) is running.

overview:
Mary Gay Scanlon seeks another term in a Delaware County–area district that leans about 15 points Democratic, and she enters as a heavy favorite. She has raised nearly $1 million and holds over $440,000 on hand, while Republican Nicholas Manganaro has raised under $10,000 with no outside spending on either side. Prediction markets give Scanlon roughly a 98% chance of winning, and no expert raters list the race as competitive.

The main caveat is the absence of public polling and expert ratings, which keeps uncertainty somewhat wide. Even so, the combination of district lean, incumbency, and a lopsided money gap makes an upset highly unlikely, and the race is rated Safe Democratic.
